title: Cairo Geniza leaf in an invented angular dash-divided script, Cambridge University Library T-S K24.37 (PGP 32699)

plaintext.source: No edition or reading found (see conditions.prior_solution).

transcription.notes: Second attempt, sign-level: two readings of every line from native-resolution windows with pixel rulers (pass 1 flattened, pass 2 CLAHE, same model, lines 5-8 of pass 2 anchored by pass 1), disagreements resolved at 3.2x, class contact sheets reviewed. final.txt is positioned and graded: 209 signs (98 firm, 72 likely, 39 doubtful; 19 of them unclassifiable ?) in 36 shape classes, 15 dash and 8 dot dividers (in transcription.txt, not in the token file). Lost zones: hole in line 6 (x 2555-2830), about 260 px in lines 3 and 7, line 8 left of x 2150, line 2 right of x 3900. Class letters are labels, not letters of a script. Replaces the first-pass 166-token, 15-class transcription (kept as transcription_first_attempt.txt).

system.summary: 8 lines of angular signs in dash- and dot-divided groups, the lower lines inside a ruled frame; 36 shape classes on the second reading, dominated by upright stems with a foot to the left (J) or right (L), long headed bars, solid blobs, boxes and brackets; system, language and direction not established (right-to-left probable from margins and ink pooling).
system.notes: Recto: 8 sparse lines (top line, three stacked lines, three framed lines), stems with feet, hooks, boxes, arches, dash and dot dividers; verso only a mirrored ink offset.

prior_solution.where: No reading found: Princeton Geniza Project record read 24 Nov 2026 (no transcription, translation or bibliography; input by Alan Elbaum 2021); 25 Nov 2026 Geniza literature survey and thorough sweep (PGP dump, Bohak 2010, Cambridge Genizah blog, Elbaum 2022 Q&A) name no reading; web search 24 Nov 2026 finds no record; DECODE harvest in the repository has no entry. Bohak, Elbaum and Zinger not asked.

conditions.human_role: The user asked for an attempt on the two Cairo Geniza leaves picked by the 25 Nov 2026 sweeps; no human transcription or hint.

solution.what: PGP record 32699 (description 'mysterious writing ... might be mirror-image Hebrew script. Needs examination', no tags, no bibliography, no related documents; entered by Alan Elbaum 2021), the 25 Nov 2026 sweeps (which first marked it a probable mirror imprint, then re-viewed it as an invented angular alphabet), web search, DECODE grep: no reading; not in Bohak's list.
Fetched both CUDL IIIF images in region tiles at native size by curl (recto 5673 x 6438, verso 5757 x 6413).

PGP's mirror-image idea: the verso (second image) shows a faint mirrored ink offset of the recto lines (ink transfer or bleed-through), which explains the note; the recto signs themselves were flipped horizontally in a crop and do not become recognisable square Hebrew by eye (inconclusive for single letters).

First-pass shape-class transcription of the recto from background-flattened crops (2 per line): 8 lines (line 1 at the top, lines 3-5 stacked, 6, 7 and 8 inside a ruled frame), 166 tokens of 15 classes (14 plus ? for blots; 152 classifiable), 24 dividers (dashes and dots). Lines 1, 6, 7 are firm; 2-5 and 8 are rubbed or faint (counts +-20%). Classes merge look-alike signs; direction not established.

Class statistics (13 classes without ? and small curls): IC 0.118 (uniform 0.077), entropy 3.26 of 3.70 bits; repeated 2-/3-/4-grams 28/7/0 against shuffle means 27.8/7.6/0.9 (z 0.1/-0.3/-0.9); H(next|prev) 2.35 vs shuffle 2.53, z -2.8 (the only departure from chance, plug-in estimate on 125 tokens); no repeated dash group among 31; dash-group lengths mostly 1-5 with a few runs of 9-15 where dividers are missing.

Compared with T-S K24.19 (viewed): no overlap in repertoire (Bohak's upright ring, x, 9 and H signs against K24.37's L/J stems, boxes, dashes). Compared with K24.24 by eye: different hand, ink, shapes and layout; only dot dividers and a zigzag shape are shared. Concluded two separate leaves, not one text (best evidence, not proof).

Added lang/ models he-tanakh and ja-from-arabic. Many-to-one monoalphabetic annealing of the 14 classes (? dropped) with dividers as word breaks, both reading directions, 4 restarts x 2000 steps: he-tanakh real -3.645 / -3.637 against shuffled nulls mean -3.685 sd 0.111 (z 0.4); ja-from-arabic real -3.044 / -3.127 against -3.150 sd 0.076 (z 1.4 / 0.3). The Arabic-model output degenerates to alif-lam strings, a sign of overfitting, not language.

Same annealer on 12 stretches of model-language text of equal length enciphered by a random many-to-one map onto 14 classes: control means -2.64 (he) and -2.37 (ja), separating from the shuffled nulls by z 9.5 and 10.2. So a clean 14-class monoalphabetic text of this length would have been detected; the real class stream is indistinguishable from its shuffle. Control text overlaps the model's training corpus (upper bound on detectability).

Looked for repeated dash groups and repeated sign runs that could hold a formula (basmala, greeting, divine name): none repeated as a whole group; repeated class runs are only 3-4 signs (J b b three times). A letter-opening formula could not be tested at class level.

Looked for other images of the leaf: the CUDL viewer JSON lists only two pages (1r, 1v; textDirection 'L' is a viewer default), IIIF ids -00003 and -00004 return 404, the PGP record shows only image 1; no raking-light, multispectral, older photograph or second shelfmark image exists in either source. Refetched the recto at native size (5673 x 6438) by region tiles.

Pass 1 of the sign-level transcription: every line cut into 700-px flattened windows (pixel ruler on each) read at 2.1-2.5x, one record per sign with x position, shape class, grade and a note (pass1.txt): 206 signs in about 34 classes, shapes split finely (stems by foot side, brackets, boxes, cups, blobs, bars, diagonals). A sign-by-sign coarse first pass had given 166 tokens in 15 classes.

Class review: contact sheets of 18 exemplars per class (J 31, b 29, c 30, B, R, U, V, I, L, D, K, W, X) viewed side by side. J kept whole (continuum of flat, hooked and long thin feet); c split into o (solid blobs) and c; b split into long headed bars and short bars d; V split into wedges and thin short diagonals; e merged into o. The three K signs and four B signs are identical shapes across lines 1, 6, 7 and 5-8.

Pass 2 with different enhancement (CLAHE), 1.6-1.8x, window edges offset: lines 1-4 re-read afresh, lines 5-8 re-viewed and confirmed (partly anchored by memory of pass 1, same model, not an independent reader). Diff sign by sign: 222 signs agree, 6 differ in class (L1 2380 and 4225, L2 3900, L4 2310, L6 3857, L8 3683), 1 in pass 1 only, 4 in pass 2 only. Each resolved on 3.2x tiles (changes_from_pass2.txt); doubt list per sign in doubts.txt. Final: 209 signs, 98 firm, 72 likely, 39 doubtful. Against the first attempt 65% of its tokens map to a compatible class, 19% to a different one, 14% involve a ?; 47 new signs (22%).

Reading direction from stroke order and layout: right ends of lines 3-8 sit at x 4770-4975 (sd about 55 px) against the right frame rule while the left ends scatter over x 1520-1835 (sd about 125 px); long bars carry the heavy head at the right and thin to the left (14 of 16); leftward feet dominate (J and Jd 33, L 8). Compatible with right-to-left writing; no smears show stroke order and the same ink pooling can come from rightward strokes, so the direction is probable, not established. I (stem) ends the left side of lines 1, 2, 4, 5.

Statistics on the new transcription (? dropped): 190 signs, 36 classes (14 with one or two examples), IC 0.065 (uniform 0.028), entropy 4.40 of 5.17 bits; repeated 2/3/4-grams 33/7/1 against shuffle means 27.3/3.4/0.2 (z 1.9/1.9/1.6); H(next|prev) 2.49 vs 2.56 (z -1.2); one repeated 4-gram, c J L R, twice in line 5 (x 1870-2195 and 3440-3760); no repeated dash group beyond the single stem. First attempt: 125 signs, 13 classes, IC 0.118, repeats 28/7/0, z -2.8 on H(next|prev).

Re-ran the first attempt's many-to-one monoalphabetic annealer (tsk2424/attack.py, 36 classes onto 22 letters, dividers as word breaks, 6 restarts x 3000 steps, 12 shuffled nulls) on the new tokens: he-tanakh real -3.551 forward / -3.502 reversed against nulls -3.715 (sd 0.095, max -3.575), z 1.7 / 2.3; ja-from-arabic -3.142 / -3.084 against -3.250 (sd 0.081), z 1.3 / 2.1; firm and likely signs only, he-tanakh reversed z 2.8, forward 1.3. A shorter run (3 x 1500) gave z 5.4 / 4.0 with under-converged nulls and is not used. No readable output.

Same annealer on 12 stretches of model-language text of equal length enciphered by a random many-to-one map onto 36 classes with the real layout: control means -2.12 (he) and -2.15 (ja), separating from the shuffled nulls by z 16.9 and 13.5 (14.1 on the firm and likely subset). A clean monoalphabetic text of this length and class count would have shown; the real stream is inside the range of its shuffles. Control text overlaps the model corpus (upper bound).

Compared blind reading 3 (pass 1, 218 marks, 57 unmerged labels, direction right to left) with transcription.txt (36 classes): the sign inventory is unstable between readers; no consensus run was made.

Dash groups of transcription.txt: 31 groups of 1-24 signs, none repeats except the single stems I and ?, so dashes do not behave as word breaks. Flip test on crops of line 7: no square-Hebrew letter forms; signs read as a rapid pseudo-script.

Annealer without word breaks (attack.py --noword, ja-from-arabic, 4 x 2500, 8 controls): real -2.393 forward / -2.363 reversed against nulls -2.488 (sd 0.067), z 1.4 / 1.9; control separation only z 3.0. he-tanakh not run (no corpus copy in this worktree). No readable output.

Viewed nine neighbouring leaves (K5.7, K24.19, K24.23, K24.24, Misc.10.60, 11.91, 22.218, ENA 3207.17, CUL Or.1080 J277) and scanned PGP records 32670-32708: none shares the K24.37 sign set or carries a sign table; K24.19/23/24/37 are the only cipher or mystery leaves in box K24. Bohak 2010 and 2011 not accessed (proof-of-work check); no Syriac, Coptic, Samaritan or Ibn Wahshiyya tables found to test.

outcome.method_basis: No reading: the system is not identified; a sign-level transcription (36 shape classes, 209 signs) exists, but monoalphabetic language-model attacks on it score within the range of shuffled controls.
outcome.notes: In progress. Sign-level transcription done twice (second attempt of 24 Nov 2026); doubtful signs listed in doubts.txt; the next test is a blind third reading and Hebrew-letter candidate sets per class.
